changes_made.explanation: Removed overly specific task description, generalized LLM reference since specific model not mentioned, clarified output descriptions. The paper focuses on using LLMs for data augmentation through paraphrase generation for sexism detection.
Added macro F1-score which is explicitly mentioned as the evaluation metric used for all tasks (A, B, and C). The paper does indeed use automatic metrics to evaluate classification performance.
No LLMs are used as judges/evaluators in this paper. LLMs are only used for generating synthetic data, not for evaluating outputs.

The paper analyzes existing human annotations from the EDOS dataset but does not conduct new human evaluations of their generated outputs. They rely on the original dataset annotations and automatic metrics.

overall_notes: This is primarily a sexism detection/classification paper that uses NLG for data augmentation purposes. The core task is classification (sexism detection), not NLG evaluation. The NLG components are used to generate synthetic training data to improve classification performance. The extraction was mostly accurate but missed the macro F1-score metric used for evaluation.
